title: Same-floor graph routing
contract: Euclidean edge lengths unless distance_m is supplied; directed edges remain directed; distance divided by constant speed gives travel time.
limitations: Reference cases do not prove all graph shapes or validate surveyed distances.

title: Door and corridor straight-passage width
contract: Passage requires max(robot width, oriented payload width) <= effective edge width, with 1e-9 m numerical tolerance. Effective width is the minimum of the corridor and its endpoint door openings. Select the shortest passable route.
limitations: No safety clearance, door height, opening time, door leaf swing or swept turning footprint is modelled. A door restricts both full incident edges.

title: Route profiles and task restrictions
contract: Route profiles define clean, dirty and shared access: shared sections belong to each applicable profile. Profile and task allow-lists are unioned; empty lists mean unrestricted; edge pairs are directed. The dirty task label selects the dirty profile only when no explicit profile is supplied. Unknown effective profiles reject scheduling instead of becoming unrestricted. Empty approach, charging and idle-return travel remain unrestricted by profiles. Returns use return_route_profile or their label fallback; seeded waste returns may inherit the outbound profile. Generating profile edges from selected nodes includes both directions of two-way corridors. Each multi-stop leg intersects the effective permissions of payloads currently onboard; empty intersections remain forbidden. Clearance uses only the oriented payloads currently carried. Profile/task unions remain per-task; batch groups retain profile and dirty-label compatibility.
limitations: No physical contamination-state model or empty-journey profile selector. Task allowances can widen a profile intentionally. Reference node, edge and lift intersections are verified; seeded-return and wider profile interactions remain incomplete. Static checks do not resolve every effective generation or runtime-return profile; the engine checks effective tasks before scheduling. Existing saved edge lists are not automatically changed; regenerate deliberately if reverse directions were omitted.

title: Corridor lane capacity
contract: Current two-way capacity approximation uses half corridor width and both loaded length and width to choose one or two concurrent lanes.
limitations: Not a directional keep-right lane model; no geometric junction conflict or overtaking verification. Length-based lane fitting is conservative.

title: Swept turns and multi-point manoeuvres
contract: Planned shared geometric model with explicit radius, pivot and reversing parameters.
limitations: Existing local manoeuvre drawing uses an approximate radius. Do not treat it as verified full-route swept geometry or steering dynamics.

title: Scheduled generation and override precedence
contract: Global disable wins. Enabled group/department rules can run under disabled category defaults. Group payload overrides category values and suppresses that department's standalone override. Separate groups are separate services. Category-wide zone capacity policy cannot be overridden. Category-only generation runs only without groups or department overrides. Polling includes the final partial interval at the inclusive demand horizon; released work can complete afterward. Clock schedules and timeframe slots now use exact calendar events. Effective pre-start releases are excluded; department opening adjustments can retain an occurrence across midnight. Consumption polling cadence is unchanged.
limitations: Exact release does not imply immediate assignment: resource waits, staff handoffs and configured staggering remain. Minute clock parsing is retained; fractional timeframe slots retain calculated precision. The wider generation-mode and calendar interaction matrix is still incomplete.

title: Consumption, threshold, waste and timeframe generation
contract: Generation derives demand from schedules, configured consumption and department assignments; tracked containers have separate balances.
limitations: Independent boundary cases remain for every mode, recurrence, waste volume, partial-day and timeframe allocation. Preview must distinguish runtime-dependent demand from fixed schedules.

title: Task assignment, priorities and deferral
contract: Deferral deadline starts at the original release and applies until assignment; zero means unlimited. Idle parking is excluded. One reference delivery takes 2 + 10/2 + 2 = 9 seconds.
limitations: Priority fairness, all candidate-limit interactions and end-of-run incomplete-task reconciliation need further reference cases.

title: Returns, staff handoffs and exchanges
contract: Returns and staff transfers retain physical payload identities. Same-container servicing records an arrival outside storage and returns the original bin; finite exchange stock is unaffected. Destination dwell and walking contribute separately to availability.
limitations: Existing regression coverage is broad, but a complete independent return/profile/staff-shift matrix is outstanding.

title: Location reservation capacity
contract: Reservations occupy half-open intervals. A request starts at the earliest time that existing simultaneous occupancy stays below capacity throughout its duration.
limitations: These tests cover location reservations, not all lift, edge, staff or junction contention.

title: Inventory bays and payload instances
contract: Flexible bays accept matching dimensions with permitted plan rotation. Exchange deliveries and returns can represent different physical instances. Same-bin service arrivals do not create stored stock or consume a finite bay. Strict multi-stop deliveries require distinct compatible bays. Existing active claims cannot be overwritten. Temporarily full compatible bays wait until capacity is released or the original deferral deadline expires; without a deadline they can remain pending.
limitations: Reference cycles verify instance conservation and storage counts; system-wide conservation over long mixed workflows still needs independent evidence.

title: AMR types, slots and multi-stop routing
contract: Robot and slot dimensions constrain payload compatibility; multi-stop tasks share movements. Each multi-stop leg intersects the effective permissions of payloads currently onboard; empty intersections remain forbidden. Clearance uses only the oriented payloads currently carried. Profile/task unions remain per-task; batch groups retain profile and dirty-label compatibility. Rejected serial multi-stop commits restore touched reservations, inventory claims, lift operational state, battery/energy and impact counters. Rejected individual and idle-return commits also restore task destinations, robot state and appended charging records.
limitations: Slot combinations, fleet contention, routing optimality and all orientation combinations need further cases. Greedy pickup-first stop ordering is not a complete tour search; conservative corridor energy still uses the full-batch aggregate. Swept slot geometry is not verified. Joint physical empty-bin exchange claims and atomicity beyond route planning remain separate audits.

title: Battery, charging and idle returns
contract: Opportunity charging is optional and admits idle robots progressively. Rejected charging-route plans retain departure occupancy and restore charger claims, lift operational state and robot targets. Estimates do not assign a target charger. One in-place charge reference verifies 5 kWh / 1 kW = 18000 seconds.
limitations: Independent energy balance, charger queues, thresholds and charging efficiency calculations remain outstanding. Charger travel reservations and travel-energy accounting need explicit acceptance cases; route-plan rollback does not cover an exception later during event publication.

title: Lift simulation and movement exports
contract: Lift transfers and empty repositioning are distinct movements; multiple tasks on one movement do not multiply its count.
limitations: Export tests do not prove all lift scheduling, dimensions, failures, queues and travel-time calculations.

title: People movement and congestion
contract: Configured people occupancy applies speed factors to corridor travel.
limitations: No dedicated independent reference suite for overlapping profiles, ramp shapes or time windows yet.

title: Scenarios and resource availability
contract: Scenario events modify selected resource availability and speed over configured periods.
limitations: Dedicated boundary and recovery tests remain outstanding.

title: Run period and simulation time
contract: Simulation times are elapsed seconds relative to the configured start datetime. Individual exports may round times.
limitations: Timezone/DST, all midnight boundaries and all end-of-run semantics need explicit policy and reference cases. tick_rate is not a physical accuracy setting.

title: Reports and metric reconciliation
contract: Tasks, AMR journeys, payload movements and lift trips are separate measures. Missing metadata must not be fabricated.
limitations: Complete metric-to-event traceability and reconciliation for every report measure remain outstanding.

title: PDF/DXF drawing import and export
contract: Drawings provide floor-scaled underlays; topology uses explicit world coordinates.
limitations: No automatic verified obstacle extraction from drawings. Broader import failure/scale coverage remains.

title: Editor validation and dialog behaviour
contract: Structured preflight reports severity, object, consequences and navigation; edits invalidate reports and acknowledgements. Launcher snapshots checked inputs and warnings per run. Existing dialogs remain available. Shared compressed edit history supports undo/redo of completed configuration and canvas edits.
limitations: Incremental checks, not a complete schema. Generation rule references need effective precedence resolution; legacy findings may lack exact navigation. Undo groups existing dialogs and callbacks; individual command migration and systematic accessibility coverage remain outstanding.

title: Visualiser and task investigation
contract: Playback uses event records; failure navigation locates the affected destination.
limitations: Legacy playback remains supported. Results investigation adds evidence IDs and task timelines; shared swept trajectories and full report reconciliation remain outstanding.

title: Portable project, history and integrated application
contract: Compressed .amrproj stores deduplicated drawings and revisions with atomic saves and restore. Separate 30-second recovery copies preserve unsaved configurations and available drawings; Save/Discard/Cancel protects open/close. JSON export serves existing tools; results remain external. Project runs saves, checks and simulates a frozen saved revision in a separate process, with external results bound to project, revision and software identities.
limitations: Persistent external-run references inside project metadata, a full project tree, integrated playback/reporting and history/recovery retention cleanup remain outstanding. Run relinking and custom locations are session-local. Storage/discovery operations are synchronous. The legacy launcher retains its machine-specific workspace path.

title: Demand preview and rule provenance
contract: Frozen planned-task preview with filters, timetable, effective rule settings, no-work explanations and simple independent schedule reconciliation. Runtime-dependent totals remain unknown.
limitations: Complex calendars, runtime inventory/returns and full waste field-source attribution are not independently verified. Preview IDs are not simulation event IDs.

title: Results timelines and run evidence
contract: Recorded task outcomes and metric definitions link to contributing events. New logs retain stable event/journey identities, frozen inputs and source fingerprints; old logs expose missing evidence. Completed and failed task sets reconcile with bound run summaries. Payload service arrivals close transfers without adding inventory; logs declare this capability so older logs do not claim zero service activity.
limitations: Planned segments do not prove execution. Payload pairing can be incomplete; wait causes are not additive; full PDF metric reconciliation and large-log pagination remain open.
